hypotheses.label: AVAILABILITY-PAY
hypotheses.basis: The mines left CLR for ERS because ERS pays a fixed availability price for capacity it almost never calls, and that beats being dispatched for money.
hypotheses.test: ers $/MW-yr >= clr_as + clr_energy $/MW-yr AND ERS deployment < 5 h/yr
hypotheses.observed: ers $42,840 vs clr_as $9,691 + clr_energy $24,667 = $34,358; ERS deployed 0 h/yr (9 deployments since 2007, none since 2023-09). Ceiling check: the whole MW sold as NSRS at $3.65/MW-h for all 8,760 h is $31,974/MW-yr, which ERS still beats -- and ERCOT caps no CLR's AS share

hypotheses.label: ZONAL-SETTLEMENT
hypotheses.basis: The mines left because CLRs are dispatched and settled at zonal prices, which is punitive at structurally cheap (Panhandle/West) nodes.
hypotheses.test: sign test on (zonal LZ_WEST DAM price - nodal DAM price) across the structurally-cheapest settlement points; plus the timing of the fix
hypotheses.observed: median zonal minus nodal = $12.32/MWh over 99 cheapest-decile settlement points (mean DAM <= $28.43/MWh) in 2025-04-02 to 2026-08-30 DAM (provisional: one month); 100% positive, sign-test p = 3.16e-30; nodal settlement would therefore PAY these loads, so the grievance runs the other way and NPRR 1188 is a reason to stay. NPRR 1188 (nodal pricing for CLRs) PUCT-approved November 2024; nodal pricing and DAM energy/AS co-optimisation for CLRs; ERCOT implementation scheduled January 2027, project initiated after RTC go-live -- approved before the 2025 exit, not after it. Load-zone settlement applies to a mine whether or not it registers as a CLR, so it is not a differential reason to deregister.

hypotheses.label: RISING-OBLIGATION-COST
hypotheses.basis: The mines left because the cost of carrying CLR obligations -- telemetry, PFR, the patent licence, AS delivery risk -- went up.
hypotheses.test: count of rule/legal changes on record 2024-2026 that RAISED the cost of being a CLR
hypotheses.observed: 0 cost increases on record; 5 changes that LOWERED it: NPRR 1131 (implemented August 2024) let CLRs provide ONLINE Non-Spin instead of offline only, ending the requirement to hold consumption at the award level until manual deployment; CLR patent dispute resolved April 2025; licences now free, removing the exclusive-rights barrier to registering as a CLR; RTC+B go-live 2025-12-05 lets a CLR sell AS in real time, skip the day-ahead market, and buy out of day-ahead AS positions without a failure-to-provide penalty, removing the main CLR risk (energy-price exposure against an AS obligation); NPRR 1188 approved November 2024 will settle CLRs at nodal rather than zonal prices, curing the Panhandle basis complaint; NPRR 1244 approved November 2024 drops the primary-frequency-response requirement for CLR registration

hypotheses.label: DOUBLE-DIP
hypotheses.basis: ERS is stackable: the same MW is paid to stand by, still self-curtails on price, and still dodges the 4CP peaks. A CLR's AS award and SCED bid curve spend that MW.
hypotheses.observed: ERS stack $124,233 vs CLR stack $91,085 per flexible MW-yr (difference $33,148); the ERS leg costs 0 h/yr of curtailment

decision_c: No — the business as underwritten dies with 4CP. The killer is §25.193(d)(2)(B), the non-coincident-peak leg of the minimum billing demand, not 12CP. What carries a business is interconnection access sold as availability.
what_would_have_to_change: Drop or soften §25.193(d)(2)(B), the NCP leg, in the adopted rule (Project 58000; SB6 deadline 2026-12-31)
Weighted-average minimum billing demand with the contracted/NCP weight ≤ 0.43, or a ratchet below 30% of contracted demand
A curtailable / non-firm interconnection class exempt from the floor — the FERC-ordered kind (June 18 2026 show-cause; RM26-4) — adopted by the PUCT
Behind-the-meter gas or storage cheap enough to break even against a $30/MWh grid (today: breakeven capex $15–385/kW vs $2,550/kW quoted)
